scoring.priority_rule: P0 is an active correctness or trust failure; P1 blocks coherent module completion or promotion; P2 materially weakens authoring or migration; P3 is polish.

items.title: Consolidate source-only material under the canonical module taxonomy
evidence: chapters/legacy/README.md and the canonical Module 06, 07, and 09 overviews
_toc.yml, myst.yml, and notebooks/manifest.json canonical notebooks/course paths; notebooks/labs/ is empty
affected_workflows_or_users: authors integrating fixed-income, derivatives, risk, or portfolio text
items.observed_symptom: Useful sources retain old numbers that collide with the 11-module curriculum.
items.potential_impact: New text can be attached to the wrong module or duplicate an existing lesson.
items.engineering_risk: Renaming paired notebooks without coordinated manifest, TOC, link, and cell-id updates can break publication.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A promoted page uses legacy numbering while the roadmap and navigation identify a different subject for that number.
items.recommended_next_action: Preserve canonical notebooks/course numbering and the explicit legacy boundary; update the plan, both TOCs, the manifest, local links, visual-asset ownership, and Jupytext pairs atomically for future promotions.
validation_criteria: No promoted path uses a legacy module number.
Both TOCs, the manifest, and all local links agree after each move.
make publish-check passes.

items.title: Complete the quantitative foundations and executable macro branch
affected_workflows_or_users: students entering time-series and valuation lessons
authors relying on probability, inference, regression, simulation, macro, or FX prerequisites
items.observed_symptom: Module 02 publishes a strong time-series branch without the broader methods promised by its title, while Module 03 is mainly narrative.
items.potential_impact: Later modules must repeat prerequisites or assume concepts that the book has not taught.
items.engineering_risk: New notebooks may introduce overlapping notation, data contracts, or modeling helpers.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A later lesson invokes inference, regression, simulation, parity, or scenario analysis with no canonical prerequisite page.
items.recommended_next_action: Treat Bayesian, clustering, nowcasting, and currency-overlay work as optional extensions; preserve chronological validation, explicit benchmarks, versioned data, and module handoffs.
validation_criteria: Every new page declares prerequisites and a non-duplicative role.
Executable examples use versioned data and pass fresh execution.
Module statuses and next-text targets are updated.

items.title: Author the four modules that currently have no reusable book text
items.observed_symptom: Financial statements, corporate and equity valuation, alternatives, and the capstone exist only as roadmap targets.
items.potential_impact: The published book remains structurally incomplete even when its current pages build successfully.
items.engineering_risk: Large content drops can bypass the intake boundary and create inconsistent terminology, citations, or navigation.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A module is marked published before its overview, sequence, evidence, and assessment contract are complete.
items.recommended_next_action: Route future filing-backed, manager-level, or capstone cases through make new-content and promote only with citations, rights evidence, the plan, both TOCs, and the manifest updated atomically.
validation_criteria: Each module has an approved overview and explicit lesson sequence.
Claims and datasets pass citation, provenance, and rights review.
Promotion changes the plan and both TOCs atomically.

items.title: Replace generic checkpoint boilerplate with lesson-specific assessment
evidence: all 71 published lesson sources in notebooks/manifest.json
items.observed_symptom: Many notebooks end with the same general prompt and rubric.
items.potential_impact: Assessment does not reliably demonstrate mastery of the lesson-specific objective.
items.engineering_risk: Bulk edits to generated ipynb files would be overwritten by the canonical percent sources.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A notebook passes structural validation while its checkpoint can be answered without using the lesson method.
items.recommended_next_action: Keep lesson-specific practice and rubrics aligned with learning objectives; retain the semantic content validator and fresh notebook execution for every future promotion.
validation_criteria: Each checkpoint names a lesson-specific calculation or interpretation.
Each rubric maps visibly to a learning objective.
Notebook-pair and fresh-execution checks pass.

items.title: Add prerequisite and next-step links inside the published learning path
evidence: all 71 published sources in notebooks/manifest.json contain prerequisite and handoff or next-step sections
canonical module overviews and reading or mastery sequences
scripts/book_content.py semantic marker checks and scripts/check_book_links.py
affected_workflows_or_users: authors deciding where new text belongs
items.observed_symptom: The TOC orders pages, but the pages themselves rarely state prerequisites or the next recommended lesson.
items.potential_impact: Readers can miss conceptual dependencies and authors can introduce duplicate explanations.
items.engineering_risk: Unvalidated relative links can break when legacy material is renumbered.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A student enters an advanced notebook without the required concept, or a link points to a pre-migration path.
items.recommended_next_action: Preserve prerequisite and handoff blocks when adding or renumbering lessons, and run make check-book-content plus make check-book-links before promotion.
validation_criteria: Every promoted lesson has a clear role and handoff.
All local links pass make check-book-links.
No link targets a legacy module number after migration.

items.title: Keep Jupyter Book 2 provisional until output and deployment parity are proven
items.observed_symptom: The Book 2 configuration has structural page parity but is not the production build.
items.potential_impact: Premature promotion could lose output fidelity, citations, links, or deployment behavior.
items.engineering_risk: Two build systems can drift if page and validation parity are not enforced.
items.concrete_failure_mode: The production command changes before Book 2 renders every published output and passes equivalent deployment checks.
items.recommended_next_action: Run the parallel Book 2 evaluator and record visual-output, citation, redirect, link, and deployment parity before changing the production build.
validation_criteria: Page order remains identical to the production TOC.
Published notebook outputs and citations are visually and semantically equivalent.
A deployment rehearsal passes with the candidate configuration.

items.title: Correct semantic contradictions in the published learning path
evidence: tests/test_market_data_observations.py, tests/test_market_risk.py, tests/test_module2_visuals.py, tests/test_quantitative_foundations.py, and tests/test_time_series_diagnostics.py
affected_workflows_or_users: students interpreting the integrated market case
students comparing ARCH, GARCH, VaR, and Expected Shortfall
items.observed_symptom: Published pages previously passed structural checks while validating a retired path, treating calendar-filled values as observations, plotting or naming the wrong fitted model, or changing the sign of VaR.
items.potential_impact: Readers can reproduce a technically successful but financially mislabeled result.
items.engineering_risk: Notebook pairs and shared quantitative helpers can preserve inconsistent behavior after a prose-only correction.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A clean clone fails setup or a published table or figure reports a different model, sample, or risk sign from the surrounding explanation.
items.recommended_next_action: Retain provider-date, no-look-ahead, stationary-parameter, 95%-diagnostic-band, positive-loss VaR and Expected Shortfall, standardized-Student-t, deterministic Jupytext, and fresh-kernel regression checks in the publication gate.
validation_criteria: Setup checks use notebooks/course and pass in a clean clone.
The integrated case executes the scope declared by its overview.
Module 02 empirical models use provider-dated Banxico FIX observations rather than forward-filled alignment rows.
ARIMA, ARCH, and GARCH outputs are bound to the model and sample named by each page.
ACF and PACF figures use declared 95% bands and dashboard parameters cannot enter a non-stationary state.
All VaR and ES equations and outputs follow the positive-loss contract.

items.title: Revalidate source-only quantitative results before promotion
affected_workflows_or_users: students using curve, portfolio, and market-risk calculations
reviewers relying on generated figures and tables
items.observed_symptom: Some source-only calculations omit cash flows, infer curve factors from heterogeneous rates, accept invalid correlation matrices, or use incorrect portfolio formulas.
items.potential_impact: Promotion would turn known mathematical defects into canonical instruction.
items.engineering_risk: Correcting notebook prose without testing reusable helpers can leave the numerical defect active.
items.concrete_failure_mode: A promoted lesson produces an invalid discount factor, factor interpretation, tangency portfolio, or covariance result.
dependencies: src fixed-income, term-structure, market-risk, and portfolio helpers
items.recommended_next_action: Preserve cash-flow completeness, explicit compounding, positive-semidefinite covariance, fully invested portfolio weights, and factor-label invariants with focused tests and fresh-kernel execution for future quantitative changes.
validation_criteria: Curve construction prices every contractual cash flow or fails explicitly.
Rate conventions round-trip under a declared compounding basis.
Portfolio covariance inputs are positive semidefinite and weights satisfy their constraints.
Every corrected source runs from a fresh kernel.

items.title: Align empirical sample, construction, and reuse-rights disclosures
evidence: data/snapshots/metadata.json coverage, carry methodology, and conservative rights note
items.observed_symptom: Declared sample endpoints differ from analyzed snapshots, constructed carry indices are not explained in the lesson, and provider access does not establish redistribution rights.
items.potential_impact: Readers cannot reproduce cross-page comparisons or determine whether a snapshot is safe to redistribute.
items.engineering_risk: Refreshing a snapshot can silently change lesson dates, units, and rights assumptions.
items.concrete_failure_mode: Two pages claim to use the same panel but analyze different periods, or a committed dataset is treated as licensed without evidence.
items.recommended_next_action: On every snapshot refresh, regenerate coverage and carry metadata, display actual observed boundaries, and re-review provider terms before making any redistribution claim.
validation_criteria: Every empirical page reports the actual inclusive sample window.
Constructed indices declare formula, calendar, and base convention.
Snapshot metadata distinguishes access method from redistribution rights.
No publication text claims a license that has not been verified.
